F1: salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts` calls `prisma.credential.update` but never imports `prisma`, so it fails type checking and throws a ReferenceError when that line runs.
F2: parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns the whole `safeParse` result, so Google stores `{success, data}` as `key`, and the next `googleCredentialSchema.parse(credential.key)` fails.
F3: both computed keys turn into the same literal key `"[object Object]"` and `z.object` strips unknown keys, so `expires_in`/`refresh_token` are lost (Zoom then works out `expiry_date` from undefined).
F4: the delegated branch returns a raw Fetch `Response`, but Google reads `res.data.access_token` and Zoho reads `tokenInfo.data.error`, so both break when sharing is enabled.
F5: appStoreMetadata` is keyed by directory name (`googlecalendar`, `office365video`), not by slug (`google-calendar`, `msteams`), so looking it up by the database slug returns undefined and the webhook sends back a 404.
F6: Bigin passes `credentialId` as the third argument, which gets sent as `calcomUserId`, so the sync endpoint is asked for the wrong user.
F7: when a response has no refresh token, the placeholder `"refresh_token"` gets merged over the real stored token in Office365 (and assigned directly in Zoom), which breaks the next refresh.
